unmapped_findings: Hardness of the 19Al alloy reaches its maximum of 917.8 HV at 600 °C/10 h (not at the extracted 575 °C/6 h condition, which gives 835.4 HV); the paper's fracture-toughness (KIC = 3.5 MPa·m1/2 for 19Al), nanoindentation hardness (10.4 ± 1.3 GPa), intrinsic β-Mn hardness (12.5 ± 0.4 GPa) and TEM interface analyses (Figs. 11–12) all refer to the hardest samples (19Al = 600 °C/10 h, 15Al = 600 °C/6 h, 17Al = 575 °C/6 h), not to the 19Al 575 °C/6 h condition.

For the 19Al alloy, the amount of Al dissolved in β-Mn measured by SEM-EDS in its hardest sample is 17.5 at.% (Mn 36.2 at.%, Cu 2.6 at.%), which the paper links to solid-solution strengthening of β-Mn; this composition is reported for the hardest (600 °C/10 h) sample rather than the 575 °C/6 h condition.

Increasing Al content slowed the β-Mn precipitation kinetics in these alloys: for the 19Al alloy the α→β-Mn transformation was complete only after ~10 h at 550 °C, untransformed α was still observed after 3 h at 575 °C, and at 600 °C and above the transformation completed within 1 h.

The Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steel series shows an ultra-wide adjustable hardness from 253.4 HV to 965.6 HV through simple aging; the 15Al alloy (Fe-35.2Mn-15Al-5.2Cu) achieved an ultra-high specific hardness of 141 HV·cm3/g. No specific-hardness value is reported for the 19Al 575 °C/6 h condition.
